findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — [P1, confidence 100] `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` now persists the `{ success: true, data: ... }` safeParse envelope through `data: { key }` instead of credential fields, so even a normal non-sync refresh makes the next service construction fail `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — [P1, confidence 100] `return response;` returns an unread Fetch Response in sync mode while its callbacks return provider-specific objects, so Google's `const token = res?.data;` produces undefined and HubSpot's `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken`/`expiresIn` are absent, breaking refresh despite a successful sync endpoint response.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — [P1, confidence 100] `[z.string().toString()]: z.number(),` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional(),` create literal object keys rather than wildcard field schemas, so Zod strips actual expiry and provider fields from sync responses and Office365 persists its old expired `expires_in`, repeatedly refreshing instead of honoring the returned expiry.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — [P1, confidence 100] `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT) {` chooses the reduced schema globally although `refreshOAuthTokens` bypasses sharing for credentials without a userId, so team Office365 credentials refreshed directly with Microsoft lose the real returned refresh token and are overwritten by `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";`, making their next direct refresh fail.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — [P2, confidence 100] `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", {` now forces a token-endpoint request for every client construction even with a valid access token, making all Salesforce operations fail during token-endpoint outages while the resulting connection still uses the old `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token,` and may refresh a second time.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — [P2, confidence 100] `const reqBody = appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body);` has no validation-error handling (nor do the decrypt/JSON parse operations below), so an authenticated caller submitting a missing field, malformed ciphertext, or invalid decrypted JSON receives an unhandled 500 instead of a non-retryable client-error response.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — [P1, confidence 100] `await prisma.credential.update({` references an identifier with no import or declaration in this module, so type-checking fails and a successful Salesforce refresh throws ReferenceError before constructing the client.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:3 — [P1, confidence 75] `import type { IntegrationOAuthCallbackState } from "../../types";` (also in encodeOAuthState.ts:3) resolves to app-store/_utils/types after the extra oauth directory was introduced instead of app-store/types, leaving both OAuth helpers with an unresolved type dependency.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:47 — [P1, confidence 100] `await prisma.credential.create({` runs for any accepted team member and returns before `await throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state?.teamId ?? null, userId });`, allowing a non-admin to install team credentials, including their own Stripe payment account, through a crafted OAuth teamId.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — [P1, confidence 75] `body: new URLSearchParams({` sends only `calcomUserId: userId.toString(),` and `appSlug,` with no authentication or signature, so a sync endpoint reachable by other callers that accepts this request cannot distinguish Cal.com from an attacker requesting another user's access token.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:3 — [P1, confidence 75] `import type { IntegrationOAuthCallbackState } from "../../types";` (also in encodeOAuthState.ts:3) resolves to app-store/_utils/types after the extra oauth directory was introduced instead of app-store/types, leaving both OAuth helpers with an unresolved type dependency.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the files decodeOAuthState.ts and encodeOAuthState.ts are being moved from `packages/app-store/_utils/` to `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/`. The import statement `import type { IntegrationOAuthCallbackState } from "../../types";` would resolve from `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/` going up two directories to `packages/app-store/types`. This is the correct path - the types.ts file exists at `packages/app-store/types` (as evidenced by the original import `from "../types"` when the files were in `_utils/`). The finding claims it would resolve to `app-store/_utils/types` but that's incorrect - `../../types` from `_utils/oauth/` goes to `_utils/../types` which is `app-store/types`. The relative path adjustment from `../types` to `../../types` is correct for the directory move.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — [P1, confidence 75] `body: new URLSearchParams({` sends only `calcomUserId: userId.toString(),` and `appSlug,` with no authentication or signature, so a sync endpoint reachable by other callers that accepts this request cannot distinguish Cal.com from an attacker requesting another user's access token.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that refreshOAuthTokens.ts sends a request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body, with no authentication headers or signature. Looking at the diff, the webhook endpoint (app-credential.ts) validates requests using CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header, but the refreshOAuthTokens function that calls the sync endpoint doesn't include any such authentication. This means the sync endpoint would need to be secured separately, and if it accepts unauthenticated requests, an attacker could request tokens for arbitrary users. This is a legitimate security concern - the code sends sensitive requests without authentication.
